summary: One medium omission: the map leaves out the explicitly audited positive-definite-kernel overlap between Part C and OptimalTransport 13A. Existing generic kernel positivity and scalar Kolmogorov interfaces should be reused, while continuity, universality and signed-Radon-measure separation remain consumer obligations. The three retained links, four existing overlaps and seven cited pinned declarations pass the checks described in the report.

Narrow semigroup/representation terms gave 12 records; a broader kernel/positivity/heat/GNS screen gave 100. Screened 429 roadmap Markdown files (72 matching lines in seven files) and reserved identifiers. Positive quadratic forms, height pairings and Gram operators were distinguished from positive-definite functions and kernels.

No sibling research link map records Part C with OT13A or its parent. AUDIT-06 explicitly records this duplicate; the focal examined entry only reads OT10/11/14 and omits it.

Read Feydy et al., PMLR 89 (2019), PDF pages 2-5, specifically the kernel energy definition, universality condition, Theorem 1 and its main-text argument. Used it to delimit kernel positivity versus universality, not to claim a complete audit of the paper or its supplementary proofs.

Adversarial checks retain the distinction between proximal and linear resolvents (factor tau^-1), heat evolution in total variation versus L1, arbitrary involutive-monoid positivity versus the group bound, and finite Laplace measures versus endpoint differentiability. The two-point constant kernel is PSD but neither universal nor separating for signed measures.

findings.claim: The complete map omits the generic positive-definite-kernel reuse/duplication boundary requested by OT13A item 4. The reviewed library audit explicitly identifies this pair, and no sibling link map records it. The omission leaves the consumer's 'first build' wording unqualified despite existing arbitrary-index kernel positivity and scalar Kolmogorov infrastructure. This finding is limited to the missing interface record; it does not claim that universality, signed-measure separation or Sinkhorn theory is already implemented.
findings.evidence: content/tau-ceti/OneParameterSemigroups/README.md, Part C, lines 216-217 exports 'The **PD-function ↔ PD-kernel** equivalence' and 'the GNS/Kolmogorov decomposition'. content/tau-ceti/OptimalTransport/README.md, 13A item 4, lines 1486-1488 says 'first build continuous positive-definite and universal-kernel predicates on compact' followed by 'spaces, with universality expressed by density of kernel sections in `C(X)`, and the' and 'signed-Radon-measure energy/separation lemmas used below.' data/library-coverage.json, Part C duplicates, explicitly names #13a-static-entropic-transport. At Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174, Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean:59 defines Matrix.PosSemidef on arbitrary index types by Hermitian symmetry and finitely supported quadratic forms. At Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369, TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosSemidef.lean supplies posSemidef_iff_finite_sum, and Analysis/PositiveDefinite/Kernel/Kolmogorov.lean supplies scalar real/complex KolmogorovSpace, kolmogorovFeature, inner_kolmogorovFeature and kolmogorovFeature_dense using Mathlib RKHS.OfKernel. These actual statements were read. Feydy et al. Theorem 1 (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v89/feydy19a/feydy19a.pdf, PDF p. 3, read 2026-09-30) requires a positive universal kernel, so its consumer requires more than this existing finite-form positivity API.
findings.fix: Add an evidence-backed rescope/keep overlap between OneParameterSemigroups Part C and OptimalTransport #13a-static-entropic-transport, and update the examined entry. Specify reuse of the existing arbitrary-index Matrix.PosSemidef predicate, finite-quadratic-form API and scalar Kolmogorov bridge where needed. OT13A owns the continuous-kernel packaging, universality in C(X), signed-Radon-measure energy and separation bridge, and Sinkhorn conclusions; do not infer these from dense feature span in the Kolmogorov Hilbert space. Retain the two-point constant-kernel non-example. Do not require a monoid structure on an arbitrary compact X, rebuild the generic positivity/RKHS root, add a blanket Bochner-existence or BCR edge, or expand the upstream roadmap in place. An overlap suffices for this finding; any later directed dependency must name its narrower consumed contract and pass the normal graph checks.
